task: Pick up the box in the other room, but do not drop the key while the door is closed until the door has been opened once.

value.feedback: NO CHANGES NEEDED: Existence(target_picked_up) hard captures the commanded goal 'pick up the box in the other room', and hard Precedence(door_open, key_lost) bans key_lost before the first door_open, which is exactly 'do not drop the key while the door is closed until the door has been opened once' — key_lost is by definition a drop while the door is not open, and the 'until' phrasing lifts the ban once the door has been opened, which only Precedence expresses. Opening the door and acquiring the key are conditions, not commands, so they correctly get no Existence; both clauses trace to task sentences, priorities match the wording (no preference cue, both hard), and all propositions are declared and grounded.
